sections.text: Introduction

The purpose of this 
procedure is to provide detailed safe method for transmission lines maintenance 
staff to minimize the possibility of error causing personal injury or 
damage.
Safety Precautions

items:
A
 work permit must be issued.
Local earthing on both work sides is required.

Wear your
 safety helmet, safety belts.

sections.text: Tools and Equipment

Qty 
Tools & Equip.
1 Transmission line maintainers full body harness .
1 Anchor hook .
2 Lengths of switch to attach to the anchor hook .

1 
16 mm (5/8 in ) structure length nylon rope with a green tracer -
Ontario Hydro Central Stores number - 362-A0136.
OR
1 16 mm x 8 m (5/8 in x 26 ft) of the same nylon rope .
1 Shock absorber to attach to the back D of the body harness .
1 Fall arrester to connect the shock absorber to the rope - the current
approved model is the RTC 2300 .
1 Container for the rope .

Work
to be Carried out

Assembly
and Use Of Temporary Fall Protection Using the Nylon Rope

items:
Cut
 or select the length of rope to be used . When more than one person must
 climb the tower, a full structure length rope will likely be more convenient
 as the additional people may then use the same rope . If only one person is
 needed or if tower inspection is taking place, a shorter length of rope may
 be more convenient. When an 8m (26 ft) piece of rope is used, a knot must be
 tied at the bottom end of the rope to prevent the fall arrester from sliding
 off.

Attach
 one end of the rope to a small karabiner using an eye splice or a bowline
 knot.tape the tail of the bowline to the standing rope if this is the method
 of attachment.

Connect
 the karabiner, with the rope attached, to the hole in the anchor hook. The
 karabiner should be connected from the backside of the anchor hook so that
 it will not interfere when installing the hook on the tower

Put
 on the full body harness and attach a shock absorber to the back D
 ring of the harness. Use a small karabiner to attach the shock absorber if it
 does not have its own method of Attachment .

Connect
 the fall arrester to the shock absorber using a small karabiner.

Attach
 the tow lengths of switch together and connect them to the anchor hookm see
 figure1.

Raise
 the anchor hook , with the rope attached , and install it around a
 horizontal or diagonal structure member approximately 3 m (10 ft) above your
 position .

When
 installing the anchor hook , attach it around the larger members and where
 possible ,install the hook at the intersection of the steel members . Always
 check that the hook is well secured around the member . The anchor hook may
 be installed on ladder rungs but do not attach it to step bolts .

sections.text:
Figure 1: Climbing a Tower Using the Rope Method of Temporary Fall
Protection

When
 a full length of rope is used , the first power line maintainer may require
 assistance in raising it to the work location. When help is required , once
 past the midway mark, secure the anchor hook and lrt a second person climb
 up to the midway mark while his fall arrester is attached to the rope .
NOTE

items:
Climb
 the tower diagonals, ladder or step bolts to a level near the anchor hook.

While
 maintaining good footing, belt to a tower member or ladder using a pole
 strap .

Remove
 the anchor hook and relocate it to a suitable member within reach of the
 switch sticks, see figure 1.

Un
 belt
 from the tower member or ladder and climb to the anchor hook location.

Repeat
 this sequence until the work location is reach.

Only
 one person must use the rope for fall protection at any given time. Other
 power line maintainers must be belted to the structure while someone
 else is using the rope for fall protection.

Once
 the second person is belted in near the midway point , he can hold the
 weight and feed the rope while the first power line maintainer continues
 to relocate the anchor hook and climb to the work location .

If
 additional power line maintainers are required work on the structure , they
 may climb , one at a time , using their fall arrester on the rope already
 installed .

When
 the work is completed , each person descends in turn while his fall arrester
 is attached to the rope.

When
 everyone is off thw structure , the last power line maintainer descends to a
 location where he can still reach the bottom of the switch stick.

Belt
 to the structure and remove the anchor hook from the member and then
 relocate it to a member at approximately waist height .

Unbelt from the structure and descend to a location where the bottom of the 
 switch sticks can still be reached and relocate the anchor hook again .

This
 sequence is repeated to the base of the structure.

sections.text:
Safety
Summary

The
following hazards and precautions are emphasized to highlight sum of the safety

considerations
related to climbing a structure . Other hazards which are site specific or of

a
general nature must be identified during the tailboard conference before the
work begins .

Hazards 
Precautions

Body
Mechanics - do not
over reach when installing the anchor hook.
The weight of the anchor hook and rope could
overbalance the sticks .

Electrical 
 - Observe the limits of approach to energized
conductors when using the nylon rope for
temporary fall protection .

Mechanical 
 - Inspect all fall protection equipment before use.
- Replace any component in the system that has
arrested a fall .
- Always have a full structure length rope or
handline as well as karabiners available for possible
rescue at the work location .
